Design a phased implementation plan for a new feature in KasirKu (G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu, Next.js App Router + Supabase multi-tenant POS/finance SaaS, Bahasa Indonesia UI). Do NOT write any code — this is planning only, produce a structured written plan as your response text.

## Background / decisions already made by the user (do not re-litigate these)
- Roadmap item: "Sistem Finance dijual terpisah" — sell the existing Akuntansi/SDM module as its own product to businesses that already have their own POS/cashier and only want KasirKu's accounting/HR module.
- User reviewed a reference HTML prototype (D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\AkunPro_v10_1.html, "AkunPro — Sistem Akuntansi F&B") as the design+functionality target and wants that look-and-feel (dense enterprise SaaS layout, sidebar grouped nav, stat cards, pill badges) adapted to KasirKu's actual brand green (#00a651, see src/app/globals.css), NOT the reference's literal orange accent — same precedent as how the Kalkulator HPP Desktop redesign recolored a reference mockup to brand green.
- Architecture: reuse KasirKu's EXISTING Supabase double-entry accounting engine (journal, RLS, tutup buku — already built, do not rebuild).
- Lembur & THR: stay manual-nominal only, flexible — explicitly rejected the reference's automatic UU-formula calculators. NOT in scope.
- Payroll komponen-gaji settings (toggleable tunjangan jabatan/makan/transport, configurable BPJS %, kasbon tracking): explicitly deferred, NOT in scope for this plan.
- Packaging mechanism: a NEW BILLING PLAN TIER (not a new business_type, not just a marketing page over the existing bundle) — a "Finance Only" plan that gates OUT the POS/product/table nav and gates IN only Akuntansi/SDM/relevant Kas & Rekening pages, sold on the same domain with its own marketing/landing page (same pattern as /kalkulator-hpp).

## Remaining feature gap list to plan for (confirmed via codebase audit, nothing built yet)
1. New billing plan tier "Finance Only" + nav/route gating
2. New marketing/landing page for this product (pattern: /kalkulator-hpp)
3. Visual redesign of Akuntansi/SDM section toward the denser AkunPro-style layout, recolored to brand green
4. Invoice/Nota (client name, line items, DP/down payment, due date, print) — currently nothing like this exists
5. Notifikasi/Reminder center aggregating: hutang due soon, unpaid invoices, upcoming THR, unpaid payroll, contract-expiring employees — blocked on a missing `contract_end` field on employees
6. Kas Harian — simplified non-accounting cash in/out log for cashier-literacy users, likely a thin UI layer over the existing expense/journal auto-posting pattern
7. Standalone Rekap Absensi Bulanan page (currently embedded inside attendance/page.tsx, not separate)
8. Global period switcher synced across report pages (currently each page filters independently; finance/page.tsx even has an incompatible local Period type vs the shared reports/period.ts)
9. Bulk "export everything" to Excel (currently only per-page CSV exports exist)
- NOTE: Rekonsiliasi Rekening per-payment-method + merchant fee is ALREADY BUILT and already better than the reference (finance/page.tsx) — no work needed there except visual reskin.

## Codebase facts gathered from prior exploration (use these, don't re-derive)

**Billing (`src/lib/billing/plans.ts`)**: `PlanCode = "monthly" | "yearly" | "lifetime"`, flat array `PLANS`, `getPlan(code: string)`. `plan_code` stored as plain `text` (no CHECK constraint) in `public.subscriptions` (business_id unique fk, plan_code, status check in unpaid/active/past_due/expired, period_end, updated_at — migration 20260712110000_billing.sql). Today plan_code is PURELY a pricing/display concept — nowhere is it read to gate a specific feature/module, only used for the binary locked/unlocked whole-dashboard gate. RLS: subscriptions/payments only ever mutated by service-role (Midtrans webhook `src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts` or admin RPC `admin_activate_subscription`), never directly by tenant.

**Gate/lock mechanism**: `src/lib/billing/status.ts` `getSubscriptionAccess()` returns `{locked, status, planCode, periodEnd}`, locked = unpaid|expired. Enforced in `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` via hard `redirect()` to `/business/${id}/billing` before rendering DashboardShell — wraps the ENTIRE `(dashboard)` route group. Notably `/business/[businessId]/pos` lives OUTSIDE the `(dashboard)` group with its own page.tsx and NO subscription check at all (just business-existence + cashier PIN).

**Nav gating (`dashboard-shell.tsx`)**: `businessType: "fnb"|"retail"|"tiket"` is a PROP fetched once in layout.tsx (`supabase.from("businesses").select("id,name,business_type")`) and threaded to `DashboardShell`. `buildNavGroups(businessId, businessType)` (lines 52-152) is a pure function building nav-group array literals with inline ternaries/spreads to include/exclude items per type. "Akuntansi" and "SDM" groups (lines 80-106, 135-143) are currently NEVER filtered by business_type — every type sees full Akuntansi/SDM nav. A separate hardcoded "Buka Kasir" button (lines 213-222, always rendered, links to /business/${id}/pos) exists outside buildNavGroups entirely. The natural seam for finance-only gating is: fetch plan_code alongside business_type in layout.tsx's existing Promise.all, thread it the same way as a new prop, and inside buildNavGroups hide the whole "Operasional" group + the standalone POS button when plan is finance-only, keep Akuntansi/SDM/relevant Kas&Rekening as-is.

**Existing accounting page pattern** (e.g. accounting/rekonsiliasi): server `page.tsx` (async, awaits createClient(), scoped `.eq("business_id", businessId)` queries, `notFound()` guard) + sibling `actions.ts` ("use server", useActionState-style State type, re-validates ownership defense-in-depth even though RLS already enforces it, `.bind(null, businessId)` from the page, ends with `revalidatePath`) + client form component. New tables follow: migration with `create table` + RLS enable + single `private.owns_business(business_id)` policy (security-definer helper already exists, verbatim reused across every business-scoped table).

**employees table** (migration 20260711100000_employees.sql): `id, business_id, name, daily_rate, active, note, cashier_id, created_at`. No later migrations touch it. Adding `contract_end date` nullable is a trivial additive migration, zero conflicts.

**Kalkulator HPP marketing+purchase precedent**: `/kalkulator-hpp/page.tsx` (static marketing page) + `hpp-calculator.tsx` (client demo widget) + `/kalkulator-hpp/beli/page.tsx` + `beli/actions.ts` (guest checkout via createServiceClient since no session, order_id prefixed `HPP-` so the shared Midtrans webhook can branch by prefix — see route.ts). This is a ONE-TIME purchase flow though; a Finance-only plan is a RECURRING subscription like the existing monthly/yearly plans, so the more relevant precedent for the purchase mechanics is actually `src/app/business/[businessId]/billing/actions.ts` (order_id prefixed `KK-`, extends subscriptions.period_end via plan.periodDays) — the marketing-page-on-same-domain PATTERN comes from kalkulator-hpp, but the PAYMENT mechanics should follow the existing subscription billing page, not the one-time desktop-order flow.

**Period type mismatch**: shared `reports/period.ts` exports `Period = "today"|"week"|"month"|"all"|"custom"` + `getPeriodRange()` (WIB-aware). `finance/page.tsx` has its own local unexported `Period = "today"|"week"|"month"|"all"` (no custom, no shared helper reuse) — a pre-existing tech debt item, not something this feature necessarily needs to fix, but relevant if global-period-sync touches finance/page.tsx.

**Print pattern precedent**: `payroll/[payslipId]/page.tsx` + `print-button.tsx` — `print:hidden` on chrome/controls, `print:max-w-none print:mt-0 print:rounded-none print:border-0 print:p-0` on the card, plain `window.print()` button, no PDF lib. Reuse this exact pattern for Invoice/Nota print view.

## What I need from you
A phased, ordered implementation plan (not code) that:
1. Sequences the 9 gap items into logical phases (what must come before what — e.g. billing plan + gating almost certainly must come before the marketing page since the marketing page needs somewhere real to sell; contract_end field must come before the notification center; etc.)
2. For each phase, names the concrete files to create/modify (new migration filenames with placeholder timestamps, new route folders, which existing files get edited) — reuse the exact patterns above, don't invent new architectural styles
3. Flags any open design decisions within a phase that still need a user call (e.g., exact Finance-only plan pricing/name, whether the visual redesign happens all-at-once or gradually per-page, whether the marketing page needs its own distinct domain path)
4. Keeps scope honest — this is a large multi-session effort, so phases should be independently shippable/verifiable, not one giant PR
5. Notes verification approach per phase (what to check in the browser preview, matching this project's established pattern of full E2E browser verification with a seeded test account before considering a phase done)

Return your plan as clearly structured prose/lists in your response — I will read it and write the final plan file myself, so prioritize clarity and completeness over brevity.

# KasirKu "Finance Only" Product — Phased Implementation Plan

## Sequencing rationale (why this order)

The 9 gap items split into two dependency chains plus a few free-floating items:

- **Sellability chain**: billing plan tier/gating → (marketing page). Nothing else strictly depends on this, but it's the item that turns the roadmap goal ("sell separately") into revenue, so it should land early even before the product is fully polished.
- **Notification chain**: `employees.contract_end` + `purchases.due_date` (schema) → Invoice/Nota (adds its own `due_date`) → Notification center. Each step is a hard prerequisite for the next.
- **Free-floating, low-risk quick wins**: standalone Rekap Absensi page, Kas Harian, bulk Excel export. These have no dependencies on anything else and can be slotted wherever is convenient.
- **Refactor-before-reskin**: the global period switcher touches the filter/header chrome of the same Akuntansi/report pages that the visual redesign will restyle. Doing the period-sync refactor first means the redesign only has to style each page once, not twice.

Given that, here is the order I'd plan and ship in. Each phase is independently shippable and independently verifiable in the browser with a seeded test business owner account — none of them require a later phase to be "half-done" to demo.

---

## Phase 1 — Finance-Only billing plan tier + nav/route gating

**Goal**: A `finance_only`-style plan exists in the pricing model, and when a business is subscribed to it, the dashboard nav shows only Akuntansi/SDM/relevant Kas & Rekening items — no Operasional group, no "Buka Kasir" button.

**Files to modify**:
- `src/lib/billing/plans.ts` — add new `PlanCode` value(s) and `Plan` entries. Since the file already documents plans as "purely a pricing/display concept," this is additive: e.g. `"finance_monthly" | "finance_yearly"` (mirroring the existing monthly/yearly cadence) alongside a new exported helper, e.g. `isFinancePlan(code: string | null): boolean`, probably keyed off a `family: "full" | "finance"` field added to the `Plan` type rather than string-prefix sniffing — cleaner and avoids fragile prefix matching.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` — extend the existing `Promise.all` to also select `plan_code` (it's already fetching `access` via `getSubscriptionAccess`, which already returns `planCode` — likely no new query needed at all, just thread `access.planCode` through to `DashboardShell` as a new prop, e.g. `isFinanceOnly={isFinancePlan(access.planCode)}`).
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/dashboard-shell.tsx` — add `isFinanceOnly: boolean` prop, pass into `buildNavGroups(businessId, businessType, isFinanceOnly)`; inside the function, wrap the `"Operasional"` group in a conditional and conditionally omit it from the returned array; also conditionally hide the hardcoded "Buka Kasir" button block (lines ~213-222).
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/billing/page.tsx` — needs to render the new plan(s) somehow (see open decision below).

**New migration**: none required for this phase — `plan_code` is already a free-text column with no CHECK constraint, so no schema change needed.

**Open design decisions (need your call before/during this phase)**:
1. **Exact plan name(s) and price** — is it one flat "Finance Only" tier, or split monthly/yearly like the existing plans? What's the price point relative to the existing Rp99.000/Rp990.000?
2. **How does a business "become" finance-only?** Three options, ranging from least to most engineering:
   - **(C) Simplest** — leave onboarding (`src/app/onboarding/onboarding-form.tsx` + `actions.ts`) completely unchanged (still asks fnb/retail/tiket, which becomes cosmetically irrelevant for finance-only tenants since Operasional is hidden anyway); on the existing `billing/page.tsx`, just render all plans (existing 3 + new finance plan(s)) in one grid with a short badge/description distinguishing "Kasir + Akuntansi" vs "Akuntansi & SDM saja." Zero new routing/plumbing.
   - **(A) Medium** — marketing page CTA passes a query param (e.g. `/onboarding?product=finance`) that onboarding forwards to `billing/page.tsx?product=finance`, which then filters `PLANS` to show only the finance plan(s) for that first-time flow.
   - **(B) Most control** — a fully separate purchase flow mirroring `/kalkulator-hpp/beli` (own route, own server action creating business+subscription in one step), diverging further from the existing subscription-billing pattern.
   
   I'd recommend **(C)** for a first ship — it reuses 100% of existing billing plumbing, ships fastest, and can be refined later once you see whether customers are confused seeing 5 plans in one grid.
3. **Route-level enforcement vs nav-only hiding**: today `/business/[id]/pos` and the Operasional pages (`/products`, `/tables`, `/customers`, `/purchases`, `/suppliers`, `/assets`, `/receivables`) have no plan-specific check — hiding the nav link doesn't stop someone typing the URL directly. The requirement as stated ("gates OUT the POS/product/table nav") is nav-only, so Phase 1 can ship with just that. Flagging that a follow-up (redirect at the route/layout level, following this codebase's own defense-in-depth convention seen in `accounting/*/actions.ts`) may be wanted later — your call on whether that's in-scope now or deferred.

**Verification**: log in as a seeded test business owner, use the admin panel (or manual SQL) to set a business's `subscriptions.plan_code` to the new finance code, refresh dashboard — confirm Operasional group and "Buka Kasir" button are gone, Akuntansi/SDM/Rekonsiliasi remain, and that a normal monthly/yearly/lifetime business is unaffected. Manually navigate to `/business/[id]/pos` and an Operasional URL to observe current (unenforced) behavior, matching whatever was decided in decision #3.

---

## Phase 2 — Data model prerequisites for the notification center

**Goal**: Add the two missing date fields the future Notifikasi/Reminder center needs, and make sure they're actually populated (not just present) by exposing them in the existing forms — otherwise Phase 6 would ship against empty columns.

**New migrations** (placeholder timestamps, must sort after the latest existing migration):
- `supabase/migrations/20260715100000_employee_contract_end.sql` — `alter table public.employees add column contract_end date;` (nullable, additive, zero conflict per the employees migration's structure).
- `supabase/migrations/20260715110000_purchase_due_date.sql` — `alter table public.purchases add column due_date date;` (nullable, additive — the `purchases` table currently has no due-date concept at all, confirmed via `supabase/migrations/20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql`).

**Files to modify** (so the fields are actually settable, not orphaned columns):
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/employees/page.tsx` and its `actions.ts`/add-employee form — add an optional "Tanggal Berakhir Kontrak" date input, following the existing field patterns in that form.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/purchases/add-purchase-form.tsx` + `purchases/actions.ts` — add an optional "Jatuh Tempo" date input alongside the existing hutang/paid_amount fields.

**Open design decisions**: none blocking — this is pure additive schema + form wiring, following exactly the existing conventions.

**Verification**: create/edit an employee with a contract end date, create/edit a purchase with a due date, confirm both persist and redisplay correctly (list views may or may not show the new field yet — that's fine, consumption happens in Phase 6).

---

## Phase 3 — Standalone Rekap Absensi Bulanan page

**Goal**: Pull the monthly recap block currently embedded in `attendance/page.tsx` (lines ~134-159) out into its own route, so it's linkable/printable/exportable independently rather than only visible at the bottom of the daily-check-in page.

**Files to create**:
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/attendance/rekap/page.tsx` — new server page that reuses the same `recap` computation logic (month-start-to-date aggregation over `attendance` joined to `employees`), but with its own month selector (prev/next month, not day-by-day) rather than inheriting the daily page's `date` query param semantics.

**Files to modify**:
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/attendance/page.tsx` — decide whether to keep the embedded recap block as-is (for at-a-glance convenience) and simply add a "Lihat Rekap Bulanan →" link to the new page, or remove the embedded block now that it has a dedicated home. I'd lean toward keeping a link and trimming the embedded block to avoid duplicate logic drift.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/dashboard-shell.tsx` — optionally add the new route to the SDM nav group (or leave it reachable only via the link from the daily attendance page — your call).

**Open design decisions**: should the standalone page get its own CSV export (matching the "per-page CSV exports" pattern noted as already existing elsewhere) now, or is that deferred to Phase 10's bulk export? I'd suggest deferring — keep this phase small.

**Verification**: navigate to the new route, confirm the same numbers shown in the old embedded block now appear on the standalone page for a given month, confirm month-prev/next navigation works, confirm the daily attendance page still functions.

---

## Phase 4 — Invoice/Nota module

**Goal**: A genuinely new feature — client name, line items, DP (down payment), due date, print view. Nothing like this exists today; `receivables` is the closest precedent but only has a flat `amount`/`paid_amount`/`customer_id`/`description`, no line items.

**New migration**: `supabase/migrations/20260715120000_invoices.sql`
- `public.invoices` table: `id, business_id, customer_id (nullable fk to customers, or a plain text client-name field if you want walk-in/no-customer-record invoices), invoice_number (or generate on the fly), date, due_date, dp_amount, status (draft/unpaid/partial/paid — mirror the `payments.status`-style check constraint convention), note, created_at`.
- `public.invoice_lines` table: `id, invoice_id fk cascade, description, qty, unit_price, line_total (or computed client-side)`.
- RLS: enable on both, single `private.owns_business(business_id)` policy on `invoices` (verbatim reused helper), and `invoice_lines` scoped via a join/exists check against `invoices.business_id` (following whatever pattern child-line tables elsewhere in this schema use — check `journal_lines`' policy against `journal_entries` for the exact idiom to copy).

**Files to create** (mirroring the `accounting/rekonsiliasi` and `payroll/[payslipId]` patterns):

**Goal**: One period selector whose choice persists across report/accounting pages, instead of each page filtering independently. Also fix `finance/page.tsx`'s incompatible local `Period` type (`"today"|"week"|"month"|"all"`, no `"custom"`) to use the shared `reports/period.ts` type/helpers.

- The 13 files already confirmed to import from `reports/period.ts` (`ticket-reports/page.tsx`, `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, `reports/laba-rugi/page.tsx`, `reports/page.tsx`, `reports/price-trend/page.tsx`, `accounting/laba-rugi/page.tsx`, `accounting/jurnal/page.tsx`, `accounting/modal/page.tsx`, `accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`, plus the two `export/route.ts` CSV exporters) — each needs to read the "global" period from a shared source rather than (or in addition to) its own `?period=` query param.

**Open design decisions**:
1. **Persistence mechanism** — cookie (works for SSR reads on next request, simplest to reason about given this is a Server Components-heavy app) vs URL query param propagation (zero storage, but requires every cross-page link within the report/accounting section to carry `?period=`) vs client-side context+localStorage (most "sticky" UX but adds client-side complexity to otherwise-server pages). Given this app leans heavily on server components with `searchParams`, I'd lean toward the cookie approach so each page's existing `searchParams`-driven pattern barely changes — just reads a fallback default from a cookie instead of hardcoding `"today"`.
2. **Where does the switcher UI live?** — a persistent control in the topbar/shell (visible on every accounting/report page) vs. per-page as today but wired to shared state. A topbar placement is closer to the AkunPro reference's dense-enterprise feel and pairs naturally with Phase 8's redesign — worth deciding whether to build the switcher's final visual home now (Phase 7) or as a placeholder now + restyle in Phase 8.
